solution: Change the class inheritance from 'unittest.TestCase' to 'object'. According to Section 7.1 (TEST FILE ANATOMY & CONVENTIONS) of the HPX QE QAMA Scripting Best Practice Knowledge Base, all test classes in the HPX automation framework MUST inherit from 'object', not 'unittest.TestCase'. The correct pattern is: 'class Test_Suite_01_Add_Shortcut(object):'. This is the standard pytest-based class structure used throughout the HPX rebranding automation framework, as pytest does not require unittest.TestCase inheritance for test discovery and execution. Remove the 'import unittest' statement as it is not needed.

mistake_content: Added 'autouse=True' parameter to the @pytest.fixture decorator in class_setup method
solution: This is NOT actually a mistake - the 'autouse=True' parameter is CORRECT and should be KEPT. According to Section 7.1 (TEST FILE ANATOMY & CONVENTIONS) of the HPX QE QAMA Scripting Best Practice Knowledge Base, the class_setup fixture MUST use '@pytest.fixture(scope="class", autouse=True)'. This is the standard pattern used throughout the HPX automation framework. The autouse=True parameter ensures the fixture runs automatically for all test methods in the class without requiring explicit declaration in each test method signature, which is essential for initializing cls.driver, cls.fc, and flow aliases that all tests depend on. The code diff shows this was added as a CORRECTION (the comment '# GLOBAL MISTAKE: Missing autouse=True' was removed), confirming this follows the correct HPX framework convention.
